text:
customer-svc: FYI — acme-corp reported a big p99 spike on /v1/generate around 2026-01-15T14:02Z. Their trace shows an unexpected hop to ap-southeast-1 (sg) before hitting the model node. Request-id: 01FZQ7H9. Trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/01FZQ7H9

lina: thanks — can you paste the trace span list (service/region tags)?

customer-svc: pasted below (sanitized):
- client -> edge-us-west-2 (ingress-gw)
- edge-us-west-2 -> egress-gw-us-west-2
- egress-gw-us-west-2 -> peering-partner-sg (next-hop: 52.76.x.x) [unexpected]
- peering-partner-sg -> model-node-ap-southeast-1
- model-node-ap-southeast-1 -> response back via same path

customer-svc: sample repro curl we used:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Region-Hint: us-west-2" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate
```

marco: interesting — the hop to the partner SG peering looks like an egress policy choice, not a model fallback. Any recent route table changes?

jordan: also worth noting: the model instance in ap-southeast is quantized and has slower p99 on long context, so even a single cross-region hop can blow p99.

aya: @eng-infra can you check egress gateway route preferences + BGP for us-west-2 egress? Could be a BGP prepending/AS path change causing traffic to prefer the partner link.

eng-infra: looking now — pulling egress routes for gw-us-west-2: `ip route show table 220` and peering configs. Quick output: `default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0 metric 1000` and we have a static route for 0.0.0.0/0 via partner-peer (52.76.x.x) with metric 900 (priority higher) — that seems wrong. Investigating who applied that.

lina: do we have any recent config pushes? @sre-bot any config-change alerts on 2026-01-15?

sre-bot: [alert] config-push detected 2026-01-15T13:50Z -> terraform:egress-gw-us-west-2 (changed by infra-oncall). Diff: set route next-hop to partner-peer with metric 900.

marco: that explains it — route priority made partner-peer preferred for outbound internet, which causes egress to go via SG peer and then to model nodes there. Why was that pushed?

eng-infra: open ticket with infra-oncall — but immediate mitigation: change metric to 1100 so our direct internet egress is preferred. I'll run these commands on gw-us-west-2: `ip route replace 0.0.0.0/0 via 10.0.0.1 metric 1100 table 220` and `conntrack -F` after to clear stale sessions.

customer-svc: do we expect any connection resets for active customers?

eng-infra: small risk during conntrack flush, but we can do staged: update route first, wait 30s, then flush if p99 doesn't drop.

jordan: if we can't touch prod immediately, can we do a model-routing policy fallback to prefer local variants? (short term)

marco: we have a route fix already in PR: terraform://repos/infra/egress-rt/changes/457. I'm going to revert the partner-peering default route in the cloud config and trigger a rolling apply.

deploy-bot: canary apply started for infra/egress-rt (change 457) in us-west-2 at 2026-01-15T14:12Z

eng-infra: just applied route metric change on 2 gw nodes. Observing traces now.

customer-svc: re-run repro — p99 dropped from ~1.6s to ~230ms. Trace now shows: client -> edge-us-west-2 -> model-node-us-west-2, no SG hop. Request-id: 01FZQ8L2.

lina: nice. Any follow-ups?

eng-infra: opening postmortem ticket to track why PR introduced partner-peer as default for 0.0.0.0/0 — looks like a templating bug in terraform module that set partner as lower metric. Also add an alert rule for unexpected region tag in span: if >0.5% of traces for a given customer have an egress region != request region, page oncall.

marco: adding work item to infra backlog and owners assigned.

customer-svc: shared remediation notes with acme-corp and confirmed SLA impact window. They acknowledged :thumbsup:

lina: closing thread — thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :rocket:
